memo.verdict: Neutral with a bullish tilt; park, do not progress now; conviction: working hypothesis. The record parks the case until the Q2 FY26/27 print on 25 November 2026 with the re-look defined: if Q2 prints organic growth at or above zero with the adjusted gross margin at or above 40 percent excluding one-offs, and US solutions order growth holds at double digits through the ASTRO period (ASTRO opens 28 September 2026 and carries Varian's next-generation platform launch), the case moves to bullish and progresses to Early-Stage; a negative organic print, a book-to-bill below 1.0x or a gross margin below 38 percent parks it for a year. The park rule is not triggered: management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability C; the case is parked on its return and its riskiness, not on the gate. The 'Modal return' on the record's own path is about 15 percent a year over eighteen months (15.4 percent) and about 13 percent a year over three years (13.3 percent), inside the C band and below the 20 percent bar. The entry price at which the modal path clears the bar is SEK 49.6 over eighteen months and SEK 44.2 over three years, against a share price of SEK 52.55 on 28 September 2026, about 6 percent above the eighteen-month level. The record calls it a C case with an A branch: the cleared branch (margin holds and sales inflect) at about 45 percent odds returns 25.1 percent a year at eighteen months; the uncleared branch (margin holds, sales flat) at about 55 percent returns 0.3 percent a year at eighteen months and 5.9 percent a year at three years; the expected return sits at the C-D border.
case: Elekta is a margin-led self-help recovery in a duopoly runner-up, of the 'Major Corporate Change' kind, priced at the bottom of its own range. At SEK 52.55 the shares pay for the margin the new management has already printed and for nothing else; the return clears the 20 percent bar only if the top line stops shrinking, which the record puts at plausible, not probable.

The change is internal, multi-dimensional and acting. Within twelve months an outside chief executive (Jakob Just-Bomholt, August 2025, ex-Maersk, Falck and 3Shape, no product or R&D background, SEK 48m of shares bought) and an outside chief financial officer (Klara Eiritz, March 2026, from Volvo Construction Equipment) have taken more than SEK 500m out of the cost base (over 500 roles, about 10 percent, layers from nine to six, fully in the run-rate from Q1 FY26/27), put a pricing desk with floor prices and double-digit service price rises in place, cancelled SEK 2.2bn of poor orders, written off SEK 1.4bn of failed development (Kaiku wound down with a SEK 235m goodwill write-off; SEK 851m of abandoned cloud software impaired), cut R&D capitalisation from about 60 percent to about 40 percent, reorganised into five regions with full profit-and-loss accountability, replaced four of six executive committee members, refreshed the board, launched Evo (FDA 510(k) 16 January 2026; about a 30 percent premium to legacy models at broadly unchanged cost of goods) and Elekta ONE (SaaS conversion uplift above 50 percent), and set FY28/29 targets above the delivered record. The screen's rule is met twice over and every red-flag check passes. A further internal force is the shift to cash-backed earnings as the internal measure, with an EBIT cash margin of 11.4 percent reported beside the 11.2 percent adjusted margin in Q1 FY26/27, the first quarter in which the cash measure is not below the accounting one.

The external forces subtract at the moment the case needs the top line to turn. Competition tightens on both flanks (Varian's platform at ASTRO into Evo's window; United Imaging in China); supply side and macro are headwinds (Crawley GBP costs against USD revenue, a 1 percent SEK move worth SEK 32m of net profit, a 10 percent USD depreciation worth about SEK 300m of operating income before hedging, tariffs on UK-made linacs under Section 232 review, component and logistics inflation about 300 basis points); political and regulatory forces net out (Evo cleared and the CMS bundled model postponed, against EU4Health cut 35 percent and China's Class B centralised procurement); the structural demand tailwind of 6 to 8 percent a year is one Elekta is not growing with. The case therefore rests on what the company does to itself.
counter_case: Elekta is a value trap wearing a turnaround. The margin gain is a one-off from headcount and a flattering mix, not a structural change: the Q1 FY26/27 gross margin was lifted by solutions falling 9 percent and services rising 5 percent, and it reverses as hardware recovers; the pricing desk costs tenders; the margin sags back to 10 to 12 percent once the mix normalises. The company has lost share for a decade to a competitor with twice its installed base (about 10,000 systems against 5,000) and the software clinicians prefer (ARIA and Eclipse against a MOSAIQ experts call clunky and closed, cited as the reason for lost tenders in Austria and US academic centres); organic growth of about 1 percent over three years against Varian's high single digits and 10 percent over a decade; US share from above 20 percent to below 15 percent. Varian's platform at ASTRO this week removes Evo's brief technological edge and could pause US orders, which the sell-side itself flags. United Imaging, from under 10 percent to over 30 percent of China's radiotherapy market in five years, takes the Chinese volume the negative working capital (advances SEK 4.17bn, largely emerging-market prepayments) depends on. Revenue stays flat, the outer-year estimates keep falling (FY27/28 -2.5 percent over six months; FY28/29 -4.8 percent over twelve), and the multiple has no reason to leave its trough. The evidence: Q1's -2 percent organic against +0.8 percent expected; twelve quarters of misses; ten expert calls that call the software closed and clunky and Unity a commercial flop; the risks research's own reading, "a deep value trap masquerading as a turnaround story", with order growth without cash as the most dangerous deception, and a backlog that "has risen significantly over the past decade without matching top-line sales growth"; the change-forces research's "cost-cut mirage, where structural top-line erosion eventually overwhelms temporary OPEX reductions"; four of eleven brokers at Sell with targets to SEK 41; the risks research's pre-Q1 scenarios of fair-value falls of 25 to 30 percent at 40 to 45 percent probability, 50 to 60 percent at 25 to 30 percent and 70 percent-plus at 10 to 15 percent. Book-to-bill of 1.11x with Q1 free cash flow of SEK -266m and a SEK 604m working-capital outflow is the false friend's early warning. The concentrating pull is mechanical: residents train on Varian and choose Varian; the Siemens service base "dwarfs" Elekta's scale; the imaging bundle takes tenders Elekta cannot see; management says bundled deals remain rare, the experts say otherwise. The chief executive has no product background, the team is wholly new with no bench, the founder holds 30.2 percent of votes and "has always been the CEO"; the culture sits at an employee net promoter score of 8 against a target of 30 with 32 whistleblower cases in 2024/25. The new targets are "far from conservative" (Deutsche Bank) and "back-end loaded" (Jefferies) from a company whose record is the over-promiser archetype. The framework's own arithmetic says the case is broadly mediocre (24 percent of scoped attributes at B or better, an F), the top-line red flag is present now, the growth engine decelerated over twelve months, six causes for concern stand against a threshold of three, four headwinds run in the value chain, and the leading indicators arrive only quarterly. At the head of 'Investment Case' the counter-case runs the other way too: that the riskiness is priced and fading and the case is a C that should progress now; the record answers that a priced red flag is still a red flag on a case whose payoff needs the top line, that the mediocrity arithmetic is the framework's, and that the difference is two prints.

The record's concessions, at full weight: the top line has not turned and the burden of proof is on the company, not the sceptic; the Q1 gross margin was flattered by mix, which is why the FY26/27 margin is held at 13.2 percent, below the 13.4 percent consensus; ASTRO is a real risk and the sales inflection is no better than plausible; the China cash profile is a dependency; the software inferiority is asserted by several experts and not disproved; the record cannot check the framework's own error files; the odds given to the cleared branch, about 45 percent, are this hypothesis's odds turned round. The record's response: the SEK 500m is headcount that has left (over 80 percent of departures finalised by the spring), the service price rises are contractual, the software mix is structural, and the EBIT cash margin of 11.4 percent above the 11.2 percent adjusted margin refutes the capitalisation false friend for that quarter; at 11.6x with a 4.6 percent covered yield the uncleared branch returns about zero over eighteen months and 6 percent a year over three, not a loss of 25 to 60 percent, because the multiple has already fallen and the margin has already printed; the Evo data (double-digit US solutions orders, over 25 percent competitive flips, Iris imaging rated above Varian's Halcyon by a chair in California on 22 September 2026) are the first product-cycle evidence in a decade that runs the other way; the operator has done in twelve months what the previous three did not do in ten years. So the hypothesis is priced at about 55 percent, not rejected; the verdict is neutral with a bullish tilt, not bearish.
triggers: - Q2 FY26/27 on 25 November 2026: organic growth at or above zero with the adjusted gross margin at or above 40 percent excluding one-offs, and double-digit US solutions order growth through the ASTRO period, moves the case to bullish and progresses it to Early-Stage; a negative organic print, a book-to-bill below 1.0x or a gross margin below 38 percent parks it for a year.

- ASTRO from 28 September 2026: the market reaction over the following weeks is the first external test; a reported purchasing pause among major US accounts is the Alarm level; US solutions order growth below 5 percent in Q2 or Q3 FY26/27 invalidates the sales-inflection driver.

- Margin delivery: Alarm below 12.5 percent adjusted EBIT margin for FY26/27; gross margin excluding one-offs below 40 percent in a quarter is the Alarm, below 38 percent or two quarters below 40 percent the Invalidate.
- Cash backing: EBIT cash margin below the adjusted EBIT margin in a quarter is the Alarm; a widening gap for two quarters invalidates; free cash flow should turn positive by Q4 FY26/27.
- Book-to-bill: confirm above 1.05x; refute below 1.0x. China: two more quarters of order growth confirm; order growth stopping for two quarters is the Alarm.
- Consensus FY27/28 EPS up 5 percent within six months confirms; a further cut over six months is the Alarm on the outer years.
